personality_one_liner: A high-visibility, industrial-grade brutalist interface built for gloved hands and harsh warehouse lighting, prioritizing absolute legibility over subtlety.

spacing.rule: Use rigid grids, hard alignment, and exposed structure. Huge tap targets for labour use.

dont's: No glass, no blur, no gradients. Strict brutalist solid surfaces for industrial contrast.

screens.name: Login
screens.purpose: Role selection and authentication with extremely large touch targets.

states.loading: Solid monochrome spinner, black on white.
states.error: Full-width red banner with sharp black borders.

screens.layout: Vertical stack of massive role buttons (Admin, Office, Labour). Hard black borders (1.5pt) around all inputs and buttons. No soft styling.

screens.name: WarehouseHome
screens.purpose: Labourer dashboard to select Inward or Outward flows.

states.loading: Skeleton loader with sharp rectangular blocks.

screens.layout: Bento-style or full-width huge cards for INWARD (आवक) and OUTWARD (जावक). Dual-language labels on everything, where Hindi is prominent. 64pt minimum height for main CTAs.

screens.name: InwardEntry
screens.purpose: Step-by-step data collection for incoming steel plates.
screens.layout: Progressive disclosure layout. Instead of one long scrollable form, break it into vertical chunks (Dimensions -> Quantity & Vehicle -> Slip Photo). Large numerical keypad for inputs instead of default system keyboard if possible, or extremely large input fields. Theoretical weight calculation shown in a prominent high-contrast box (black bg, white text).

screens.name: OutwardEntry
screens.purpose: Select stock and log outgoing material.

states.error: Variance >0.2% flag shown in massive warning yellow banner.

screens.layout: Stock selection grid using tabular data rows (Thickness x Width x Length). Followed by Broker/Vehicle inputs. Heavy use of mono font for tabular data to ensure alignment.

screens.name: InventoryPosition
screens.layout: Dense data table. Mono font for all numbers. Strong horizontal black dividers. Grouped strictly by T x W x L. Search/Filter bar pinned at the top.

hero_warehouse.alt: Rolls of steel lined up in a warehouse

hero_plates.alt: A pile of metal boxes stacked on top of each other

instructions_to_main_agent: Prioritize extremely simple UI with large touch targets (64pt minimum for primary buttons) designed for gloved hands.
Implement Bilingual Labels (English / Hindi) prominently on the Warehouse Home and Entry screens to support labourer accessibility.
Use 1.5pt hard black borders (`borderStrong`) on all inputs, buttons, and cards. No border radius (0px) everywhere. Follow Brutalist principles.
Do not use glassmorphism, blur, or soft shadows. The warehouse environment requires absolute contrast and zero visual noise.
Break forms into step-by-step wizards rather than long scrolling screens. E.g., Size -> Quantity -> Vehicle -> Slip.
Ensure the >0.2% weight variance flag is visually aggressive (e.g., using the warning/error colors prominently).
Always use the JetBrainsMono font for numeric inputs and tabular inventory data to ensure perfect vertical alignment.
